editorial.headline: Premium Call Services: Open Nationally, Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers premium-rate telephone calls routed to agents or recorded information through premium intelligent-network access codes.
editorial.body:
Premium-call activity is a narrowly defined telephone service: the organisation of calls charged at premium rates and connected either to premium-call agents, recorded information, or both. The service operates through premium-call intelligent-network access codes. Its commercial identity therefore rests on the call service itself—its premium tariff and the way callers are directed to an agent or information recording.

Registration is open across the full business spectrum: micro, small, medium and large enterprises. That matters because the activity is not confined in the record to a particular company scale. A founder considering the code should nevertheless keep the description in view: the registered activity is the provision of premium-call services through the specified access-code mechanism, rather than a general description of communications work.

At national level, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source for that position. In practical terms, the national entry is fully open to foreign ownership within the stated ceiling; there is no lower cap in the record to qualify that conclusion.

Bali presents a different question, but not a closed door. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the large-enterprise scale, its OSS risk is medium-high or high. Bali’s status is therefore OK or higher risk, and a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today under the position recorded here. The important distinction is not an invented local ownership limit, but the activity’s risk classification at the large scale and its resulting exclusion from the moratorium’s blocked categories.
